label: GO after an unrewarded trial, when the agent still prefers a2 moderately and value is high
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1 or D2), and almost only when the previous trial was unrewarded (98% of activation mass has prev_reward == 0) and the agent goes on to choose a2 (99.9% of mass). Nearly all of it comes from trials 0-49 of the episode, and none from trial 50 onward. The model-state variables sharpen it: the policy logit diff (a1 minus a2) is moderately negative, between -10 and -4 (a2 preferred but not at the extreme), and value is high, above 7.73. Mostly this is a2 perseveration after a common, unrewarded a2 trial (S2 reached), in episodes where S2 starts good. Recorded predicate: GO & prev_reward==0 & -10<choice<-4 & value>7.73, using only observed variables (the model own value and policy outputs). Dev split: precision 0.91, recall 0.67, F1 0.77, mass recall 0.91. Without the value/choice bands (GO & prev_reward==0 & action==2), mass recall is 0.98 but precision only 0.12. It never fires after rewarded trials, when a1 is chosen, or at D1/D2. Missed activations are low-magnitude: the lowest quartile is only 27% covered by the simpler predicate. Activation magnitudes are tiny in absolute terms (max 0.002). I did not check what drives magnitude beyond the quartile coverage.

issues: Factual claim 'the unit never fires after rewarded trials' is false. GO & prev_reward==1 holds 2288 of 11171 active steps on dev (20% of active steps, 2.1% of mass) and 19% of active steps on test. These are almost all in the lowest activation quartile: 72% of bottom-quartile actives on dev and 69% on test, with 0% in the top two quartiles. This is a systematic class of weak activations (GO after a rewarded a2 trial, often at rel -3), not scattered noise. It is the main reason recall is only about 0.67.

That class can't be added to the predicate. GO & prev_reward==1 & choice<-4 & value>7.73 has precision 0.045, so the predicate itself is reasonable. The explanation should say 'strong activations never follow rewarded trials; weak ones often do' instead of 'never'.

Claims that check out: GO only (D1/D2 have 0 active steps; 'phase != GO' F1 = 0). 99.9% of mass is on action==2 (a1 is 0.09% of mass). prev_reward==0 carries 97.9% of mass. ep_trial 50+ has only 5 active steps. start_high==0 (S2 good at the start) carries 81.5% of mass. prev_common==1 & prev_action==2 carries about 82% of mass, with the remaining roughly 18% at rel -3 where the previous trial is unknown. Dev scores reproduce (P 0.913, R 0.672, F1 0.774, mass recall 0.911), and so do test scores (P 0.905, R 0.689, F1 0.782, mass recall 0.915).
The predicate uses only observed or model-computed variables (phase, prev_reward, choice, value), as claimed.

Minor: the choice > -10 bound and the 7.73 value cutoff were tuned to the quantile bins. Raising value to 7.75 raises precision to 0.95 but lowers F1 to 0.73, so the reported cutoff is near-optimal. Adding ep_trial<50 changes nothing, because value already captures the early-episode restriction.
False positives on test (874) look scattered: they are GO steps after unrewarded a2 trials with no obvious extra factor.
